'''Xie Jialin''' ({{lang-zh|s=谢家麟}}; 8 August 1920 – 20 February 2016) was a Chinese physicist.

Born in [[Harbin]], he studied physics at [[Yenching University]]. Upon graduation in 1943, Xie enrolled at [[Stanford University]], where he earned a Ph.D. in 1951. While working for the [[University of Chicago Medical Center]] in 1955, he developed a particle accelerator used to treat cancerous tumors. Later that year, Xie returned to China and helped build the country's first particle accelerator. For his contribution to the development of the 30MeV electron [[Linear particle accelerator]], Xie was awarded the Scientific and Technological Achievement Prize at the 1978 National Science and Technology Conference.<ref name="jialin-xie-wins-chinas-top-science-award"/> Xie went on to become the project director during design, development and construction of the Beijing Electron Positron Collider (BEPC), which was most notably used in precision measurement of the [[Tau (particle)|τ lepton]].<ref name="jialin-xie-wins-chinas-top-science-award"/><ref name="Measurement of the mass of the τ lepton"/> He received the [[State Preeminent Science and Technology Award]] for his work in 2011.<ref name="163ne">{{cite news|script-title=zh:国家最高科技奖获得者谢家麟逝世(图)|url=http://news.163.com/16/0221/00/BGACSN5400014AED.html|access-date=6 March 2016|publisher=NetEase|date=21 February 2016|language=zh}}</ref> Xie died on 20 February 2016 at the age of 95 in Beijing.<ref name="163ne" />

The inner [[main-belt]] asteroid [[32928 Xiejialin]], discovered by [[Beijing Schmidt CCD Asteroid Program|SCAP]] at the [[Xinglong Station (NAOC)|Xinglong Station]] in 1995, is named in his honor.<ref name="MPC-Xiejialin" /> Naming citation was published on 5 January 2015 ({{small|[[Minor Planet Circulars|M.P.C.]] 91791}}).<ref name="MPC-Circulars-Archive" />
